newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB says to open shareholders meeting to media.
newsitem.headline: DKB says to open shareholders meeting to media.

text.p: Japan's scandal-hit Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), in a move aimed at regaining public trust, announced on Tuesday that it would open this year's shareholders meeting to the media for the first time.
"The plan was among the pledges recently announced by our new president-designate," a bank spokesman told Reuters.
The bank said in a statement that its shareholders meeting, scheduled for June 27, will be open to the press via monitor screens.
It added that the action was taken as a step to reform the management of shareholders' meetings, which are often criticised for their closed nature, and to make them more transparent.

DKB has recently come under heavy fire for its suspected loans to a racketeer, or "sokaiya", who has been accused of taking illegal payoffs from Japan's top brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd. Sokaiya extort money from corporations by threatening to disrupt shareholders meetings.

Late last month, DKB unveiled a sweeping reshuffle of its top management under which its president and chairman would resign to take managerial responsibility for the bank's involvement in the racketeer scandal. Their resignations will take effect after this month's shareholders' meeting.
President Katsuhiko Kondo will be replaced by Ichiro Fujita, who is now a vice president at the bank. Another vice president, Yoshiharu Mani, will replace current chairman Tadashi Okuda.

At the time of the announcements, the bank pledged to work out steps to prevent a recurrence of any such scandal, and to open up its shareholders' meetings to the media and to set up a surveillance body composed of independent members.
